plain_english_policy: This bill changes Alabama state law to allow individuals convicted of drug-related felonies to receive federal food stamps (SNAP) and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF). Currently, under a specific provision in the U.S. Code (21 U.S.C. §862a.), such individuals are automatically ineligible if their crime involved possession, use, or sale of controlled substances. HB 214 creates an exception to this federal rule for Alabama residents by stating that these individuals become eligible immediately after they finish their prison sentence or while on probation (provided the probation is being served satisfactorily). Additionally, eligibility extends to those currently completing mandatory drug or alcohol treatment programs.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would expand access to federal nutrition and welfare benefits for a specific subset of formerly incarcerated individuals in Alabama—those convicted of felonies involving drugs. By overriding the automatic disqualification found in 21 U.S.C. §862a., the policy shifts from strict exclusion based on conviction type to conditional inclusion, allowing participation once sentencing is complete or during satisfactory probation/treatment.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representatives England, Coleman and Fields affirmatively advanced this legislation to restore eligibility for drug-felony convicts.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would provide that any person convicted of a drug related felony would be eligible for assistance under the federal temporary assistance for needy families program and the federal food stamp program upon the completion of his or her sentence..."

"Section 1. Pursuant to subsection (d) of 21 U.S.C. §862a., a person convicted of a drug related felony who is otherwise ineligible for aid under the temporary assistance for needy families program and the federal food stamp program shall be eligible for the aid upon completion of his or her sentence..."
